m: अप्य्-आ-√ हृ (Pot. अप्य् आ हरेत्) to take or assume in addition, TS.

v: tri॰ apAmidam tatra sADu saMskftaM vA yat । 1 jalasaMskfte “agrego rAjApyastamizyate” f॰ 9, 86, 45 । “apyaH apsu saMskftaH” BA॰ jalasambanDini “tvayAhitamapyamapsu BAgam” f॰ 2, 38, 7 । “apyamapAM sambanDinam” BA॰ । 3 karmaRi sADO “sa I~ mfgo apyovanargurupa” f॰ 1, 145, 5 । “apyaH karmaRi sADuH” BA॰ aptuM yogyaM vede yat hrasvaSca । 4 prAptuM yogye “yonimapyamaniSitam” f॰ 2, 38, 8 । “apyam AptuM yogyam” BA॰ ।
m: अप्य (2, 3) mf(अप्या; once अपी, RV. vi, 67, 9) n being in water, coming from water, connected with water, RV. (cf. 3. आप्य).
a: अप्य — a. [अपां इदं तत्रसाधु संस्कृतं वा यत्; अद्भिः संस्कृतं P. IV. 4. 134] 1 Connected with or coming from water Rv. 2. 38. 7; watery; consisting of, consecrated with, water (as हविः). --2 Obtainable. --3 Active, connected with sacrificial acts 1. 145. 5.
अप्यंच् — [fr. अंच्] Gone into, reaching, hidden.

m: अप्य्-√ अद् to eat off, ŚBr. xiv : Caus. -आदयति, to give more (food) to eat, AitBr.

a: अप्यदीक्षितः — N. of a celebrated Draviḍa writer, author of works on Alaṃkāra and other subjects and a contemporary of Paṇḍita Jagannātha who lived in the 16th century (written also as अप्ययादीक्षित.).
अप्यर्धं — ind. Ved. Near, in the neighbourhood.

m: अप्य्-अर्धम् ind. within proximity, near to (gen.), ŚBr. (cf. अभ्य्-अर्धस्.)
अप्य्-√ 1. अस् -अस्ति (1. pl. -ष्मसि; Imper. -अस्तु; Opt. -ष्यात्), Ved. (with loc. or local adv.) to be in, be closely connected with, RV. &c.; to belong to (as a share), RV.; ŚBr.
अप्य्-√ 2. अस् (Subj. Ā. 2. sg. -अस्या-थाः) to insert, AitBr.
अप्य्-अत्य्-√ अर्ज् (3. pl. -अर्जन्ति) to add over and above, AitBr.

v: pu॰ apa + iRa--BAve ac । 1 “apagamane 2 nASe 3 vilaye ca “svApyayAditi SA॰ sU॰ BavApyAyO hi BUtAnAM SrutO vistaraSomayA” gItA । apEtyasmAt apAdAne ac । pakzapucCasanDizu “pakzapucCAni parAgBirapyayezu” kAtyA॰ 17, 6, 7, “apyayezu pakzapucCAgrasanDizu” vedadI॰ ।
m: अप्य्-अय m. joint, juncture, Kauś.; Śulb.
pouring out (of a river), PBr.; entering into, vanishing (the contrary of प्रभव or उत्पत्ति), Up. &c. (cf. स्वाप्यय.)
a: अप्ययः — 1 Approaching, meeting, joining, juncture. --2 Pouring out (of rivers). --3 Entrance into, vanishing, disappearance; absorption, dissolution into oneself.

m: अप्य्-अय—दीक्षित m. N. of a Drāviḍa saint and writer (of the sixteenth century, author of various works, celebrated as a Śaiva, and thought to be an incarnation of Śiva; also अप्याय˚ or अप्यै˚, &c.)
